name: Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of more than five juvenile polyps in the colorectum
Multiple juvenile polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract
Any number of juvenile polyps with a family history of juvenile polyposis
Identification of pathogenic mutation in SMAD4 or BMPR1A genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of more than five juvenile polyps in the colorectum OR any number of juvenile polyps with a family history of juvenile polyposis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SMAD4 and BMPR1A mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple juvenile polyps in the gastrointestinal tract

common.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss

rare.symptomName: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia features (in SMAD4 mutation carriers)

imaging: Endoscopic visualization of multiple juvenile polyps
Barium studies showing polyp-related filling defects or intussusception
other: Histopathology showing hamartomatous juvenile polyps with abundant lamina propria and cystic glands

distinguishingFeatures: Polyps are hamartomatous but with arborizing smooth muscle
Multiple hamartomas including skin and mucosal lesions
Increased risk of breast, thyroid, and endometrial cancers

redFlags: Multiple juvenile polyps detected on endoscopy
Family history of juvenile polyposis or gastrointestinal cancer
Early onset gastrointestinal bleeding or anemia
references: Jass JR, Williams CB, Bussey HJ, Morson BC. Juvenile polyposis--a precancerous condition. Histopathology. 1988;13(6):619-30.
Howe JR, Roth S, Ringold JC, et al. Mutations in the SMAD4/DPC4 gene in juvenile polyposis. Science. 1998;280(5366):1086-8.
